title: 2023 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: Flora the frog starts at \(0\) on the number line and makes a sequence of jumps to the right. In any one jump, independent of previous jumps, Flora leaps a positive integer distance \(m\) with probability \(\dfrac{1}{2^m}.\) What is the probability that Flora will eventually land at \(10?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(a_n\) be the probability that Flora ever lands exactly on \(n,\) with \(a_0=1.\) Conditioning on the first jump, \[ a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{2^k}\,a_{n-k}. \]

We prove by induction that \(a_n=\tfrac12\) for every \(n\ge 1.\) The case \(n=1\) is immediate. If the claim holds through \(n-1,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} a_n&=\frac{1}{2^n}a_0 +\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{2^k}\cdot\frac12\\ &=\frac{1}{2^n} +\frac12\left(1-\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}\right)\\ &=\frac12. \end{aligned} \]

Hence the probability of landing on \(10\) is \(\dfrac12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(a_n\) be the probability Flora ever lands on \(n;\) condition on the size of the first jump
The recursion \(a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{a_{n-k}}{2^k}\) gives the same value for every \(n\ge 1\)
